title: Γραῦς καὶ ἰατρός
titleEn: The Old Woman and the Doctor
part: The Old Woman and the Doctor (Chambry 87 · Perry 57)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 87 (= Perry 57). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Γυνὴ πρεσβῦτις τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς νοσοῦσα ἰατρὸν ἐπὶ μισθῷ παρεκάλεσεν.
sentences.tr: Gynē presbytis tous ophthalmous nosousa iatron epi misthōi parekalesen.
sentences.l: An aged woman, ailing in her eyes, called in a doctor for a fee.
sentences.n: τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς is an accusative of respect: 'sick as to her eyes'. ἐπὶ μισθῷ, 'on terms of a fee' — the contract is stated in the first line, because the fable is about its enforcement.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ εἰσιών, ὁπότε αὐτὴν ἔχριε, διετέλει ἐκείνης συμμυούσης καθ’ ἕκαστον τῶν σκευῶν ὑφαιρούμενος.
sentences.tr: Ho de eisiōn, hopote autēn echrie, dietelei ekeinēs symmyousēs kath’ hekaston tōn skeuōn hyphairoumenos.
sentences.l: And he, coming in, whenever he anointed her, continued, while she kept her eyes shut, making off with the household goods one by one.
sentences.i: Each time he came and put the salve on her eyes, he went on carrying off the household goods, one piece at a time, while she sat with her eyes shut.
sentences.n: διατελέω takes a supplementary participle: the verb supplies only the duration, ὑφαιρούμενος the action — 'he went on stealing'. ἐκείνης συμμυούσης is a genitive absolute; her eyes are closed for the treatment, which is precisely the doctor's opportunity.

sentences.t: Ἐπειδὴ δὲ πάντα ἐκφορήσας κἀκείνην ἐθεράπευσεν, ἀπῄτει τὸν ὡμολογημένον μισθόν· καὶ μὴ βουλομένης αὐτῆς ἀποδοῦναι, ἤγαγεν αὐτὴν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας.
sentences.tr: Epeidē de panta ekphorēsas kakeinēn etherapeusen, apēitei ton hōmologēmenon misthon· kai mē boulomenēs autēs apodounai, ēgagen autēn epi tous archontas.
sentences.l: But when, having carried everything off, he had also cured her, he demanded the agreed fee; and she being unwilling to pay, he brought her before the magistrates.
sentences.n: ὡμολογημένον, perfect passive participle of ὁμολογέω, 'agreed upon'. μὴ βουλομένης αὐτῆς is another genitive absolute; the negative μή with a participle, where classical Attic would use οὐ for a plain statement of fact, is ordinary in the later Greek of these fables. The ἄρχοντες are the city magistrates before whom a private suit was opened.

sentences.t: Ἡ δὲ ἔλεγε τὸν μὲν μισθὸν ὑπεσχῆσθαι, ἐὰν θεραπεύσῃ αὐτῆς τὰς ὁράσεις, νῦν δὲ χεῖρον διατεθῆναι ἐκ τῆς ἰάσεως αὐτοῦ ἢ πρότερον· « τότε μὲν γὰρ ἔβλεπον πάντα, ἔφη, τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκίας σκεύη, νῦν δ’ οὐδὲν ἰδεῖν δύναμαι. »
sentences.tr: Hē de elege ton men misthon hypeschēsthai, ean therapeusēi autēs tas horaseis, nyn de cheiron diatethēnai ek tēs iaseōs autou ē proteron· « tote men gar eblepon panta, ephē, ta epi tēs oikias skeuē, nyn d’ ouden idein dynamai. »
sentences.l: And she said that she had promised the fee if he should cure her sight, but that now she had been put in a worse condition by his treatment than before: « for then, she said, I could see all the goods that were in the house, but now I can see nothing. »
sentences.i: She said she had promised the fee on condition that he cured her sight, but that his treatment had left her worse off than before: « Then, she said, I could see everything in the house; now I can see nothing at all. »
sentences.n: ἔλεγε governs two infinitives (ὑπεσχῆσθαι, διατεθῆναι) in indirect statement, and the ἐάν-clause keeps the mood of her original words. διατεθῆναι, aor. pass. inf. of διατίθημι, 'to have been put in a condition'. The sting is in σκεύη: the same word used for what the doctor was carrying off. Her last words are false about her eyes and true about her house, and the second sense is the one that convicts him.

sentences.t: Οὕτως οἱ πονηροὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων διὰ πλεονεξίαν λανθάνουσι καθ’ ἑαυτῶν τὸν ἔλεγχον ἐπισπώμενοι.
sentences.tr: Houtōs hoi ponēroi tōn anthrōpōn dia pleonexian lanthanousi kath’ heautōn ton elenchon epispōmenoi.
sentences.l: So the wicked among men, through greed, escape their own notice drawing the proof down upon themselves.
sentences.i: So wicked men, out of greed, draw the evidence down on themselves without noticing they are doing it.
sentences.n: λανθάνω with a supplementary participle inverts the English: the participle carries the action and the verb reports that it went unnoticed. ἔλεγχος is the courtroom word for the proof that convicts — and the case is in court.
